correctness.rationale: Uniform affine-plane hitting measure weights unit normals by width. Counting crossings of the six tetrahedral edges gives expected section vertices; Cauchy’s polyhedral mean-width identity converts this to an exact weighted exterior-angle formula. Facet normals give beta_i=2arccos(sqrt(q_i)); differentiation gives sum ell_i d beta_i=0. Since the three lengths vary locally freely under a scale constraint, the only interior stationary weighted-angle shape is regular. Explicit one-coordinate and corner limits are all strictly below the regular weighted angle. Compactness proves global uniqueness; the upper endpoint and all intermediate probabilities follow by degeneration and connectedness. The actual standalone checker was run and passed direct edge-crossing tests on 1,400,000 sampled planes, 100,000 other shape tests, and boundary probes. Finite tests are corroborative, not an infinite proof.
